record.original_question: Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of regular polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 34. Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of regular polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a partially ordered set satisfying the standard axioms (bounded, graded with rank function taking values in {-1,0,...,n}, the diamond condition, and strong flag-connectedness). A flag is a maximal chain. The automorphism group acts on the set of flags; the polytope is called regular when this action is transitive, and k-orbit when there are exactly k flag orbits.

A realization of a regular abstract polytope P is a mapping β from the vertex set of P (the rank-0 elements) into a Euclidean space V such that every automorphism of P is induced by some isometry of V; this notion extends to a mapping of all faces into the lattice of affine subspaces of V. The set of all realizations of a fixed regular polytope, modulo congruence and trivial degeneracies, carries the structure of a closed convex cone whose extreme rays correspond to the irreducible orthogonal representations of the automorphism group, giving a rich theory of realizations for regular polytopes.

Problem. Develop an analogous theory of realizations for k-orbit abstract polytopes with k ≥ 2. That is, formulate an appropriate definition of a realization of a k-orbit abstract polytope (specifying how the automorphism group, or a suitable enlargement of it acting on flag orbits, must act by isometries on the image), describe the resulting space (or cone) of realizations, identify its extremal/irreducible elements and their relation to representations of the relevant group, and establish the structural results (such as decomposition into irreducible realizations and a Wythoffian/orbit-based construction) that parallel the established theory in the regular (1-orbit) case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a research program asking for the development of a theory analogous to McMullen–Schulte's realization theory of regular polytopes, but for k-orbit polytopes. While partial progress exists on realizations in special cases (e.g., 2-orbit and 3-orbit polyhedra in ordinary space) and on representation-theoretic frameworks, no comprehensive theory of k-orbit realizations has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Presents 35 open problems on combinatorial, geometric and algebraic aspects of k-orbit abstract polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems on k-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Finite 3-Orbit Polyhedra in Ordinary Space I
status_evidence.snippet: Studies realizations of 3-orbit polyhedra in Euclidean 3-space.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for specific small k and low dimensions, but a general theory is not established.

status_evidence.title: Representation Theory and Polytopes (Ladisch habilitation)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops representation-theoretic tools for realizations of polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Representation-theoretic foundations exist but a full k-orbit realization theory is still in development.
